ai.description: This tiny frog reaches 20–29 mm. It is brown with a distinct pattern of bright, star-like white spots and possesses a granular, warty dorsal texture.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Astrobatrachus kurichiyana* is uniquely distinguished by the distinct, star-like white spots scattered across its dark, warty dorsal skin, which no similar Indian frog shares.
ai.habitat: *Astrobatrachus kurichiyana* inhabits the high-altitude, evergreen shola forests and rocky stream beds of the Wayanad region in the Western Ghats, typically above 1,000m.
ai.behavior: The Starry Dwarf Frog is primarily nocturnal and displays a unique defensive strategy by remaining motionless, using its cryptic, star-speckled skin to blend into rocky moss.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Astrobatrachus kurichiyana* is a direct-developing frog that reproduces terrestrially, bypassing the free-swimming tadpole stage. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Astrobatrachus kurichiyana* is endemic to the high-elevation evergreen forests of the Wayanad plateau in the central Western Ghats of Kerala, India.
ai.callDescription: The Starry Dwarf Frog emits a high-pitched, insect-like series of rapid, rhythmic chirps, typically heard from mossy rocks near mountain streams in the Western Ghats.
